summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube dependence, with history of dumping syndrome, post-bypass hypoglycemia, and recurrent marginal ulcers, was admitted for one week of nausea with dry heaving and diarrhea and one day of constant epigastric pain similar to prior ulcer episodes. Initial evaluation showed normal WBC and liver tests with mildly elevated lipase; she was managed conservatively with bowel rest, IV fluids (including dextrose for low fingerstick glucose), antiemetics, and analgesia while surgical causes were assessed and felt unlikely. Abdominal radiographs showed a nonspecific gas pattern and a distended bladder; MRCP demonstrated normal biliary tree and pancreas without acute inflammation. EGD revealed a marginal (gastrojejunal anastomotic) ulcer with a pigmented lesion that was cauterized; she was started on pantoprazole 40 mg twice daily and sucralfate slurry by mouth four times daily, tube feeds were restarted and tolerated, and she was discharged home with short-course oxycodone and bowel regimen, with GI follow-up in 8 weeks for repeat EGD and outpatient H. pylori stool antigen testing when able.
problems: Gastrojejunal ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
Unspecified disorder of pancreatic internal secretion
Personal history of Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus
